source.basis: Operator spec page; structured facts only, no operator prose reproduced.

reading.body:
The AUS2-AUS3 campus publishes 19 MW of IT capacity across 242,000 square feet of technical space. At 40 kW per rack, a common AI training density, 19 MW supports roughly 475 racks; at 10 kW per rack, a common colocation density, the same power supports roughly 1,900 racks. The arithmetic is 19,000 kW divided by the assumed rack draw. CyrusOne has not published a per-rack power envelope for this campus, so neither figure is the operator's claim.

The six certifications qualify this campus for specific regulated workloads. PCI DSS qualifies it for payment card data environments. HIPAA qualifies it for protected health information. ISO 27001 certifies an information security management system. FISMA qualifies it for certain federal information systems. SSAE 16 Type II documents audited operational controls. TIA-942 certifies the physical facility design against a tiered data center standard. None of these certifications are AI-specific, but FISMA and ISO 27001 together make the campus eligible for government and enterprise AI workloads that carry compliance requirements.

Among the 133 CyrusOne and other facilities mapped in Texas, only 8 have published a megawatt figure on their spec pages, and those 8 together account for 315 MW of published IT capacity. At 19 MW, this campus ranks sixth among those eight by published capacity, contributing roughly 6 percent of the published Texas total this site has read. Texas is a large and active data center market, and most mapped facilities in the state publish no capacity figure at all, so the 315 MW figure understates true installed capacity by an unknown amount.
